Dated this the 08th day of January, 2025 The petitioners in OP (MV) No.65 of 2012 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda are the appellants herein.
The respondents in the OP are the respondents.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The petitioners are the wife, child and mother of deceased Jenson.

According to them, on 29.09.2011, at about 07.30 pm, while the deceased was riding a motor cycle having Registration Number KL-45-B- 3922 along Thrissur- Chalakkudy NH and when it reached near Nellai, a car bearing Registration No.KL-17-F-5010 driven by the 2 nd respondent in rash and negligent manner hit on the motorcycle and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on 07.10.2011, while under treatment.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the them, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the MACA NO. 2144 OF 2016 2025:KER:1586 offending vehicle.
Therefore, they filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.57,41,000/-, limited to Rs.40,00,000/-.
4. The 1st and 2nd respondent together filed written statement.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A25.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.31,39,000/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
9. Heard Sri.P.V.Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants, and Sri.A.R.George, the learned Standing Counsel for the insurance company.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.

2 petitioners produced Ext.A2, copy of the charge sheet involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the above charge sheet, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.
Therefore, the 3 rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
11. At the time of the incident, the deceased was aged 40 years.
The incident was on 29.09.2011.
The appellants claimed that at the time of the accident, the original claimant was employed in Gulf as Wireman getting a monthly salary of 3,800 saudi riyal.
However, the Tribunal has fixed his monthly income at Rs.20,000/- alone.
The learned counsel for the appellants would argue that the monthly income of the deceased fixed by the Tribunal is on the lesser side.

12. As per Ext.A4 - salary certificate, the deceased was getting a monthly salary of 3,800/- saudi riyal which will come to Rs.49,818/- at the MACA NO. 2144 OF 2016 2025:KER:1586 rate of Rs.13.11 per saudi riyal.

The learned counsel for the petitioners relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and Others [2020 (3) KHC 760], would argue that towards personal and living expense  of the income alone can be deducted and as such the monthly income of the deceased is to be fixed at  of Rs.49,818/-.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and Others [2020 (3) KHC 760]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, for personal and living expenses of a person working abroad, only 50% of his income is to be deducted.
Therefore, in the light of the above decision, the monthly income of the deceased is liable to be fixed at Rs.24,909/- (1/2 of Rs.49,818).
13. The learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent would argue that out of the monthly income so fixed after deducting , another 1/3 rd is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

However, in the above decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has not made any such deduction from  already deducted towards personal and living expenses and such the above submission is not maintainable.

Since the deceased was aged 40 years on the date of death and his employment was a permanent one as revealed from Ext.A4, 30% of the income is to be added towards future prospects and the multiplier to be MACA NO. 2144 OF 2016 2025:KER:1586 applied is 15.

Therefore, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.29,14,353/-.
14.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.10,000/ towards funeral expenses and Rs.75,000/- towards loss of consortium.
In addition to the same, towards 'loss of love and affection Rs.75,000/- was awarded.

In the light of the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680], the appellants are entitled to a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% for every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the amount of compensation on account of loss of estate and funeral expense will come to Rs.18,150/- each and loss of consortium will come to Rs.1,45,200/- (48,400 x 3).

3 15.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards love and affection.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further amount for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati and Others, [(2020) 9 SCC 644].

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati and Others, [(2020) 9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the above sum of Rs.75,000/- given towards love and affection is to be deducted.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-.
In addition to the same another Rs.25,000/- was awarded towards shock and anxiety.

The learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent would argue that in the light of decision in Satinder Kaur (supra), no amount can be awarded towards pain and suffering and hence he prayed for deducting the amount awarded towards pain and suffering and shock and anxiety.

However, it is to be noted that, in the light of Section 2 of Kerala Torts (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1976, the legal representatives are entitled to claim compensation even on the head pain and suffering and such I do not find any reasons to interfere with the above argument advanced by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.

Considering the fact that the deceased died after the 10 th day of the accident, after sustaining very serious injuries and suffering severe pain, I hold that, towards the head pain and suffering, the petitioners are entitled to get reasonable compensation and therefore, it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
17.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

18. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total MACA NO. 2144 OF 2016 2025:KER:1586 compensation of Rs.31,52,853/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
Sl. No.
Head of claim Amount awarded by The amount given the Tribunal(Rs) in appeal (Rs.) 1 Transportation expenses 2000 2000 2 Damage to clothing Nil Nil 3

Extra nourishment Nil Nil 4 Medical expenses 5000 5000 5 Pain and suffering 25000 50000 6 Funeral expenses 10000 18150 7 Loss of dependency 2912000 2914353 8 Loss of estate 10000 18150 9 Loss of love and affection 75000 Nil 10 Loss of expectation of life Nil Nil 11 Loss of gratuitous service Nil NIl 12
Shock and anxiety 25000 Nil 13 Loss of consortium 75000 145200
Total 31,39,000 31,52,853 Amount enhanced 13,853 19.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd MACA NO. 2144 OF 2016 2025:KER:1586 respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.31,52,853/- (Rupees Thirty One Lakh Fifty Two Thousand Eight Hundred and Fifty Three Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation,
with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

20. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay and as per rules.
